walkthroughs.body_html: Never look directly at the Sun without certified eclipse glasses. Pinhole projection is a safe alternative. Lunar eclipses are completely safe to view with the naked eye.
Just before totality, sunlight squeezes through valleys on the Moon's edge, forming Baily's beads. One last bright spot forms the famous diamond ring effect.

For 'explain why a lunar eclipse looks red': link Earth's atmosphere refracting/scattering longer (red) wavelengths into the umbra, blocking blue. Use named phenomena (Baily's beads, diamond ring) where relevant.

options: Earth's atmosphere bends red light into the umbra
The Moon glows in IR
Mars colours it
The Sun turns red

options: Diamond ring
Penumbra
Saros
Earthshine

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse?
options: Lunar eclipses are more dangerous.
Because clouds block them.
In a solar eclipse the Moon blocks the Sun; in a lunar eclipse Earth's shadow covers the Moon.
Solar eclipses happen by day, lunar at night - that is the only difference.

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.
It is made of fire.
Because clouds block them.
Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: Eclipses happen randomly.
The Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun's apparent position.
Because clouds block them.
It is made of fire.
